//: What tools/common/check/check-traceability.py needs to know about the item's
product functions, beyond the requirements that name them as units
complete: subsystems whose low-level requirements are all written. In
one of these, a product function no requirement names, that is no
accessor and is not listed below, fails the gate: the 'no unintended
function' report is a ratchet there. A subsystem enters when its part
of the report is empty, in the slice that empties it.
check_code_in_product: functions that are checks, or serve only checks,
and live in a product file, so that no `Verifies:` tag may go on them
and the item's size counts them. Each is to move into a check file; an
entry says why it is check code and what keeps it where it is. The
target is an empty map, and the gate fails on an entry that names no
function or one a requirement names.

check_code_in_product.sched::ask_for_a_decision_here: Marks this processor's reschedule flag without making the decision: only stage 9's parked-block case (check_an_end_before_the_park, L.sched.72) asks, to have the decision pending as it parks. mark_resched is sched's own, so it stays beside it.
check_code_in_product.sched::decision_pending_here: Whether this processor's reschedule flag is still set: only stage 9's parked-block case asks, to count the tries that reached the park with the decision pending. resched_asked is sched's own, so it stays beside it.
check_code_in_product.sched::direct::uncount: Takes back one count of the fast path's per-processor counters: only stage 9's parked-block case calls it, for the park it makes itself, so that test-ipc-equiv finds every count zero with the fast path off (L.sched.61). COUNTED is direct.rs's own, so it stays beside it.
check_code_in_product.sched::pending_group_here: Which job this processor's run queue keeps processor time back for (quota::Pending): only quota_check's check_a_move_settles_the_pending_charge asks. It reads the queue under its lock, which is sched's own.
check_code_in_product.sched::bandwidth_walks: How many charges made the cpu.max walk, summed over the run queues under their locks: only cpu_check's walks_only_under_a_quota, a cost guard, asks.
check_code_in_product.object::quota::check_pending_charge: Stage 13's check of the per-queue cpu.stat charge (Pending), on private records and two slots it claims; cpu_check.rs's pending() runs it. It needs Pending's private fields, claim and release, which are quota.rs's own, so it stays beside them.
check_code_in_product.object::quota::pending_cases: The cases of check_pending_charge, and called by nothing else; in quota.rs for the same reason.
check_code_in_product.object::channel::Endpoint::reader_waitin: Whether a reader waits on an end, listed on its queue or parked by the fast path (docs/OPAQUE-KERNEL.md §9.7): only the stage-9 checks that must wake a reader once it waits ask it (write_read_check, fast_path_check, the vector check's case 15). It reads the inbox's park record, which is private to channel.rs, so it stays beside it.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::check_exception_entry: The architecture's answer to the generic boot's exception-entry check: nothing to check here, since no exception finds the kernel on a program's stack. Part of the arch interface every architecture provides.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::check_distributor: The architecture's entry to the GICv2 distributor check (arch/arm_common/gicv2/check.rs, F-50), which main.rs calls through the arch interface every architecture provides; it runs the check on a GICv2 and says it did not run on a GICv3.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::check_machine: The architecture's entry to its machine check (arch/aarch64/check.rs), which main.rs calls through the arch interface every architecture provides; it runs the check and nothing else.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::gic::enabled_for_check: Reads a line's enable back from whichever GIC driver the boot chose, for the machine check's masking case; it needs the driver choice private to gic.rs.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::gic::gicv3::enabled_for_c: Reads a GICv3 line's enable bit back for the machine check; it needs the register windows private to gicv3.rs.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::gic::gicv3::idle_line_for: Finds a GICv3 line nothing has enabled for the machine check; it needs the register windows private to gicv3.rs.
check_code_in_product.arch::aarch64::gic::idle_line_for_check: Finds a line nothing has enabled, for the machine check's masking case; it needs the driver choice private to gic.rs.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::check_exception_entry: It only runs the paranoid, syscall, gdt and trap checks' run functions, for main.rs's stage 3; it can move into a check file under arch::x86_64.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::check_switch_state: It only runs switch/check.rs's run function and prints its boot lines, for stage 9's switch-state check through the arch interface (the Arm pair answer Ok there); it can move into that check file.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::cpu::forbid_user_access: Closes SMAP's window through arch::forbid_user_access, whose only callers are user/check.rs's checks.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::cpu::permit_user_access: Opens SMAP's window through arch::permit_user_access, whose only callers are user/check.rs's checks of the window; the kernel's own user copies do not use it.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::cpu::write_breakpoint_addr: Arms a debug register; called only from arch/x86_64/paranoid/check.rs, whose breakpoint checks are its reason to exist.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::cpu::write_dr7: Enables or clears the debug registers' slots; called only from arch/x86_64/paranoid/check.rs.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::identity_map_live: Its only caller is main.rs's stage 2 check, which runs only when the boot checks.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::paranoid::debug_hook: Only a breakpoint target and counter for paranoid/check.rs's check_breakpoints_do_not_nest; every kernel #DB calls it so the check can arm a breakpoint on the handler's own path.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::speculation::refill_wanted: The x86-64 half of arch::speculation::refill_wanted_in_domain, with no product caller: the domain check's case 1 (object::domain_check) asks it whether CPUID, read again, wants the in-domain refill, so that the check does not trust the plan the switch follows.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::switch::x87_resets: Read only by the stage-9 switch-state check (arch::x86_64::switch::check), with no product caller: this processor's counts of the fast vector reset's two x87 branches, which the check must see each taken (po7-ipcM's consultant, V5 and W1).
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::cpu::xinuse_readable: Read only by the stage-9 switch-state check, with no product caller: whether XGETBV 1 may be asked, so the check knows whether the x87-left branch and the XINUSE probe can run.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::speculation::check: The x86-64 half of arch::speculation_check::check (machine::check), with no product caller: it runs VERW once to show the exit paths' operand is accepted. It reaches speculation.rs's private plan.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::speculation::clear_cpu_buf: Called only by speculation::check, to run VERW once for the boot check.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::trap::breakpoint: Its only callers are main.rs's check_breakpoint, which raises int3 twice for stage 3's check.
check_code_in_product.console::input::check: The receive ring's check (FX-0305, the `input` line), run from main.rs before the port's interrupt is installed. It fills and empties RING and reads HELD and OVERRUNS, private to input.rs; as a child module, console/input/check.rs, it could read them and verify L.console.20.
check_code_in_product.console::output::check: The transmit check (FX-0504, the `output` line), run from main.rs once tasks can wait. It reads BY_INTERRUPT, BY_WRITER, HELD and waits on WRITERS, private to output.rs; as a child module, console/output/check.rs, it could read them and verify L.console.9 and L.console.10.
check_code_in_product.early::EarlyMemory::read_physical_byte: Stage 1's check_direct_map, in stages_check.rs, reads the image's first bytes through it; nothing else calls it. It can move into a check file of early's.
check_code_in_product.early::EarlyMemory::translate: Called only by stage 1's checks in main.rs (check_early_mapper, check_no_early_window_wraps); it reads EarlyMemory's private walk state.
check_code_in_product.mm::FrameWindow::kept: A check's frame window: frames kept since it opened. Every caller is a check file; it reads Held, which reads the heap and route counters private to mm.rs.
check_code_in_product.mm::FrameWindow::report_at: Prints a window's heap and per-route movement for a failing check, through FrameWindow::report; check files only.
check_code_in_product.mm::Held::now: The frame window's settled read of free frames, slab pages and route counters, for FrameWindow and held_frames, whose callers are all check files. It reads HEAP and ROUTE_COUNTS, private to mm.rs.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::console::loop_back: Serves only interrupt remapping's checks R5 and G3's service once (iommu/check.rs): it loops one byte back through the port to its own receiver. It needs the port's registers, private to arch/x86_64/console.rs, so it stays beside them.
check_code_in_product.arch::x86_64::loop_back_console: The x86-64 hook iommu::remapping::LiveLine::loop_back names for checks R5 and G3 (iommu/check.rs): it runs console::loop_back with the port quiet. Registered from console_receive_irq with the line's other hooks, so it stays beside them.
check_code_in_product.console::input::arm_check_byte: Serves only checks G3 and R5 (iommu/check.rs): it arms the receive path to take the check's looped-back byte once and keep it out of the ring, so the console thread cannot take and echo it before the check looks (FX-1012). It needs CHECK_BYTE, which receive reads under the ring's lock, private to console/input.rs.
check_code_in_product.console::input::check_byte_taken: Serves only check R5 (iommu/check.rs): it says whether the receive path has taken the armed byte, R5's wait condition. It needs CHECK_BYTE, private to console/input.rs.
check_code_in_product.console::input::disarm_check_byte: Serves only checks G3 and R5 (iommu/check.rs): it stops the receive path taking the armed byte and says whether it took it, which is what each check requires. It needs CHECK_BYTE, private to console/input.rs.
check_code_in_product.console::input::take_check_byte: Serves only check R5's not-observable arm (iommu/check.rs): it takes a looped-back byte delivered after R5 stopped waiting for it off the front of the receive ring, so it never reaches a reader. It needs the ring, private to console/input.rs.
check_code_in_product.console::output::with_port_quiet: Serves only checks R5 and G3 (iommu/check.rs): it holds the port's transmit side quiet, under the port's lock, while one byte is looped back. It needs the port lock and its ring, private to console/output.rs.
check_code_in_product.iommu::Domain::provoke_interrupt: Serves only checks R1 to R3 (device/check.rs): it clears the unit's faults and registers the interrupt fault the check is about to provoke. It needs the domain's private fault-clearing loop, as Domain::provoke does for DMA.
check_code_in_product.iommu::record_provoked_interrupt: Serves only checks R1 to R3, through Domain::provoke_interrupt: it records the stream and reason a check provokes and says so. It needs PROVOKED_INTERRUPTS, private to iommu.rs, which provoked() reads.
check_code_in_product.iommu::remapping::open_check_window: Serves only checks R1 and R2 (device/check.rs): it opens the window inside which a delivery of the check vector 0xFC is the check's, not stray. It needs the window's statics, private to iommu/remapping.rs, which the vector's handler reads.
check_code_in_product.iommu::remapping::close_check_window: Serves only checks R1 and R2: it closes open_check_window's window. Beside it for the same reason.
check_code_in_product.iommu::vtd::check_planted_completion_err: Serves only the stage 10 check of a completion error (iommu/check.rs check_completion_errors, L.iommu.48): it plants ICE in the unit's software mirror of FSTS and drives two invalidations through it. It needs the unit's mirror and counters, private to vtd.rs, so it stays beside them.
check_code_in_product.iommu::vtd::leave_queue_on_and_stop: Serves only the stage 10 check of a queue firmware left on (iommu/check.rs check_firmware_left_on, L.iommu.51): it puts a unit's queue in the state such firmware leaves it in, then calls the product path stop_firmware. It needs the unit's registers and frames, private to vtd.rs, so it stays beside them.
check_code_in_product.mm::claim_frame: Takes back a frame a check has just given up (smp/check.rs, user/rmap_check.rs), to prove it was free; no product caller.
check_code_in_product.mm::count: Counts frames per allocation route into ROUTE_COUNTS. Called on the product allocation paths, so it cannot move, but only checks read what it writes (Held::now, and user_tables_given_back for smp/check.rs's table check).
check_code_in_product.mm::frame_state: What the frame allocator records for a frame, for mm/check.rs's frame-0 check and user/edge_check.rs; no product caller.
check_code_in_product.mm::print_frame_delta: Prints which way a check's frame count missed, for a check about to fail; called only from check files. Nothing private keeps it in mm.rs; it can move to mm/check.rs with FrameWindow.
check_code_in_product.mm::unlinked::UnlinkedTables::frames: The frames a list holds, for smp/check.rs's check that an unmap's tables are still held; it reads the list's private links.
check_code_in_product.object::as_if_draining_elsewhere: Runs a check's closure as though another context were draining disposed objects (object/check.rs, block_ring/check.rs). It sets the DISPOSING flag dispose reads, which is private to object/mod.rs.
check_code_in_product.object::process::Exit::for_check: An end no process has, for object/pin/check.rs's budget checks; it needs Exit's private constructor.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::answered: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace (block_ring/trip_check.rs). Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. It sits in block_ring's complete() under the disk's state lock, which is what keeps it in product code.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::arm: Raises the seam's depth-1 trace and zeroes its counts; its only caller is block_ring/hop_check.rs.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::bell: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, on the ring task's bell to the driver. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::count: Counts switches, root writes, IPIs and device interrupts for the seam's trace, called on those product paths. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it, and only trip_check reads the counts.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::counted: Reads the trace's counts for block_ring/trip_check.rs, its only caller.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::disarm: Lowers the seam's depth-1 trace; its only caller is block_ring/hop_check.rs.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::done: Ends a traced trip and hands its stamps to block_ring/trip_check.rs, its only caller through hop_check.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::interrupt_queued: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, in Line::fire before the packet is queued. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::issued: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace: the check calls a read. Its only caller is block_ring/hop_check.rs.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::name: Records which wait queue a traced trip uses; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::now_here: Reads the counter and the processor for a stamp; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::on_ring: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as the ring task puts a request on the ring. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::port_rung: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, in port_queue on the ring's kernel port. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::port_taken: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, in port_wait on the driver's port. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::queued: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as a read is queued. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::reader_running: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as the reader runs again. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::ring_running: A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as the ring task runs. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::slept: Counts sleeps on the traced queues ended by a wake or by the recheck, called from WaitQueue::wait_until_deadline. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it, and only trip_check reads the counts.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::stamp: Stores one stamp if the traced trip has reached it; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed.
check_code_in_product.sched::trip::store: Writes a stamp slot; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed.
check_code_in_product.smp::next_job: The work run_everywhere handed out that a secondary has not done yet. Only stage 4's checks hand work out (smp/check.rs); secondary_main, product code, calls this in its wait loop until the scheduler takes the processor over, so it stays beside that loop and the JOB state both read.
check_code_in_product.smp::run_everywhere: Runs a function on every online processor at once and waits for each: how stage 4's checks run on every processor, and nothing else calls it. It writes the JOB state secondary_main's product loop reads through next_job, so moving it into smp/check.rs would leave the product loop reading a check file's state.
check_code_in_product.vmap::check_failed_device_map: A check, called from mm/check.rs's check_vmap, that a device mapping failing part way leaves nothing mapped. It uses vmap.rs's private reserve, release and map_reserved; moved into a check file it verifies L.mm.52.
check_code_in_product.vmap::check_invariants: The arena's consistency check, called from mm/check.rs's check_vmap; it reads the private ARENA. Moved into a check file it verifies L.mm.53.
